name: GSFC GEVS unit-level protoflight thermal-vacuum cycling (< 1.33e-3 Pa, AFT +/-10 C, 4 h plateaus, <= 1 C/min)
plain_name: Prove a NASA spacecraft part keeps working through hot and cold cycles in space-like vacuum
description: Unit (component) protoflight thermal-vacuum test per NASA GSFC-STD-7000B (GEVS) section 2.6: 8 thermal-vacuum cycles at the allowable flight temperature range +/-10 C, 4 h hot/cold operational plateaus, transition rate up to 1 C/min, chamber pressure below 1.33e-3 Pa after the electrical discharge checks, with the unit powered and functionally tested.
keywords: Prove a NASA spacecraft part keeps working through hot and cold cycles in space-like vacuum

requirements.rationale: Thermal-vacuum cycling requires an evacuated chamber.
Section 2.6.3.2.4: chamber pressure less than 1.33e-3 Pa (1e-5 torr).
Items electrically operational during pressure transitions undergo an electrical discharge check; the unit is powered and tested through feedthroughs.
Optional: Table 2.6-1 suggests transitions up to 1.0 C/min; a facility able to ramp at 1 C/min keeps the test schedule.
Optional: unit hot and cold operational plateaus last at least 4 h.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
